title: Add throughput SLO evaluator for Dedicated (sliding window + summary export)
author: Aisha Bello
description:
Motivation: We need a single canonical evaluator for Dedicated throughput compliance that (a) computes SLI over sliding windows, (b) applies the Dedicated-specific exclusions consistently, and (c) exports a small, stable summary that the dashboard + incident tooling can consume. Today we have ad-hoc queries in Grafana and a one-off notebook used during SLO metric exploration; they disagree on windowing and don’t encode exclusions (throttling/backpressure) consistently.

What this PR does: Adds a new evaluator implementation `DedicatedThroughputEvaluator` that computes per-deployment throughput SLI and SLO compliance over sliding windows and exports summaries to the toolkit’s standard outputs (Prometheus gauge + JSON summary artifact + optional BigQuery row format). The evaluator consumes the canonical per-deployment throughput time series emitted by the serving stack (deployment_id/model/region labels) and produces: (1) `slo:dedicated_throughput:compliance` (0/1) by deployment_id + tier, (2) `slo:dedicated_throughput:budget_remaining` in [0,1], (3) `slo:dedicated_throughput:window_achieved_tps` and `:window_floor_tps` for debugging, and (4) a compact summary payload used by the burn-rate alert generator.

SLO semantics (encoded here): SLI = achieved_tokens_per_second / committed_floor_tokens_per_second, evaluated over a 30-minute rolling window with 1-minute step. Achieved TPS is computed from `tokens_streamed_total` and `request_latency_seconds_count/sum` only for eligible requests. Exclusions applied: requests rejected due to customer-configured concurrency/quotas (e.g., 429 with `reason=customer_throttle`) are excluded from both numerator and denominator; requests routed to an explicitly unsupported model/version (per catalog metadata) are excluded and surfaced as `eligibility=unsupported_model` in diagnostics; the first 10 minutes after a deployment transitions to READY are excluded (warmup), tracked as `eligibility=warmup_grace`. Server-side admission control rejections (e.g., `reason=redwood_overload_shed`) are NOT excluded (these should count as SLO impact). Window alignment is left-closed/right-open and uses server timestamps to avoid client clock skew.

Exports: Adds `--export-format prometheus,json,bq` to `slo-toolkit evaluate` and a new default JSON artifact `dedicated_throughput_slo_summary.json` containing per-deployment status, budget remaining, primary failure reason (if any), and the top 3 diagnostic dimensions (model, region, rejection reason) for the window.

Tests: Adds unit tests for windowing math (step alignment, gaps), warmup exclusion, customer throttling exclusion, and regression coverage for streaming token accounting (ensures we use the post-fix counter semantics; see note below). Adds a small golden test for JSON summary stability to protect the dashboard consumer.

Notes / dependencies: This evaluator assumes streaming token accounting is not double-counted. If you’re running it against pre-fix metrics you may see inflated achieved TPS. The serving-stack fix is tracked separately; evaluator includes a guardrail metric `slo:dedicated_throughput:token_counter_suspect` when it detects impossible TPS given shape caps.

Rollout: Ship behind `SLO_EVAL_DEDICATED_THROUGHPUT=1` in the toolkit runner. Initial consumers will be the Dedicated SLO dashboard and the burn-rate alert generator (PR #329).
commits: windowing: add generic sliding-window aggregator w/ gap handling
dedicated: implement exclusions (warmup grace, customer throttle, unsupported model)
export: add json summary artifact + prometheus metrics
tests: coverage for streaming/non-streaming counters and alignment
docs: add evaluator usage + sample output
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): Can you clarify why customer throttling is excluded but Redwood admission control is not? Also, do we treat warm pool as the same as READY transition?

Aisha Bello (author): Yes—this matches the SLO doc semantics: customer-side throttling (their configured limit) should not count against Redwood’s ability to serve. Redwood admission control is explicitly intended to protect floors and is considered a Redwood-side miss if it sheds when the customer is within their committed floor. On warm pool: we key off deployment state transition to READY in control plane events; warm pool time before READY is not counted because we only start evaluation once READY is true.

Rafael Mendes (review): Windowing alignment looks right, but the step size being 60s means we can miss short sharp dips. Is that acceptable for the burn-rate alerts?

Aisha Bello (author): Burn-rate is computed over the same rolling windows; with 1m step we still capture dips that persist for more than one step. The intent is to avoid overreacting to single-sample noise. The raw achieved TPS metric is still available at higher resolution for incident triage.

Allison Grant (review): Please keep exported summary stable. Can we add a golden test and document schema fields so dashboards don’t break?

Aisha Bello (author): Added `tests/golden/dedicated_throughput_slo_summary.json` and documented the schema in `docs/evaluators/dedicated_throughput.md#summary-schema`.

Sergio Costa (review): For dashboard drilldowns we need model and region in the summary. Also can you include a `primary_failure_reason` so we can group panels?

Aisha Bello (author): Done. Summary now includes `dimensions` list (model, region, reject_reason) and `primary_failure_reason` enum (below_floor, warmup_grace, unsupported_model, insufficient_data).

Sean Gallagher (follow-up): The guardrail `token_counter_suspect` heuristic—what’s the cap reference?

Aisha Bello (author): Uses shape-level caps from config (conservative) keyed by `shape_class` label when present; otherwise falls back to a default max derived from historical H100/L40S envelopes. This is only a diagnostic signal and does not change compliance.

Resolution: Approved after adding summary schema docs + golden test and renaming `exclude_customer_throttle` -> `exclude_customer_config_throttle` for clarity.
